verification_test: Record an inherent critical intervention (stopper replenishment into Grade A) and a corrective non-critical one; confirm the post-intervention glove-sampling rule fires only for the critical one.

requirement: Grade A air supply is air through a filter qualified to give Grade A total-particle quality, without a requirement for continuous particle monitoring or Grade A viable limits; it protects fully stoppered, not yet crimped vials.
system_implications: Zone master data must distinguish 'Grade A zone' from 'Grade A air supply' so the EM rule engine does not demand continuous particle monitoring or Grade A viable limits at a clean-process capping station, while still recording its air supply status.
verification_test: Configure the capper as 'Grade A air supply'; confirm the batch EM plan does not require continuous particle counting there but does show air supply status.

clause: Glossary: Operator; Manual aseptic processing; Closed system; Local isolates
requirement: 'Operator' includes anyone in the processing operation (set-up, filling, maintenance and other associated personnel); manual aseptic processing covers hand compounding, filling, placing or sealing of open containers of sterile product; a closed system keeps the product unexposed, is sterilised after connections are made (for sterile products), stays closed until the operation ends and excludes RABS/isolators; local isolates are representative site organisms from Grade A/B EM, personnel monitoring or positive sterility tests.
system_implications: Qualification gates apply to every 'operator' role including maintenance; product/process master flags 'manual aseptic' and 'closed system' use these definitions to select APS rules (9.39) and background-grade rules (8.130); local-isolate library entries come from EM/PM/sterility identifications and are used in GPT and APS positive controls.
verification_test: Confirm a maintenance engineer entering Grade B during a batch is subject to the same gowning/APS gate as filling operators.

requirement: Facility and equipment design expectations (smooth impervious surfaces, no hard-to-clean recesses, low-shedding materials, sealed ceilings, no sinks/drains in Grade A/B, trapped drains elsewhere, observation windows/cameras, up-to-date equipment descriptions and P&IDs, utility installation records, no exposed pipework in cleanrooms) are verified through facility qualification, not batch execution.
system_implications: No direct eBMR function; the eBMR relies on the room/equipment qualification status (AN1-031, AN1-034, AN1-042). Traceability entry only, so the requirement matrix is complete.
verification_test: Traceability review: confirm these clauses map to the qualification-status check rather than to execution steps.

requirement: Senior management oversees the state of control; risk-management outcomes are reviewed regularly, during change, for significant emerging problems and in the periodic product quality review; CCS effectiveness forms part of management review; utility, defect and EM data are trended.
system_implications: The eBMR must store execution data in structured, queryable form (interventions by type/count/duration, hold times achieved, defect counts by code, EM links, filter test values, cycle results, deviations) and provide cross-batch exports/dashboards to feed PQR, CCS review and management review.
verification_test: Export 12 months of interventions per line by type and duration; confirm data are complete and match the batch records.

requirement: Contamination controls for microbial, endotoxin/pyrogen and particle sources are interrelated; although usually assessed, controlled and monitored one by one, their combined effectiveness should be judged together.
system_implications: Besides per-record checks, the batch review must offer a consolidated contamination-control view (timeline overlaying interventions, EM/particle data, DP/air alarms, hold times, sterilisation and filter results, personnel events) so reviewers judge the batch as a whole rather than as isolated passes.
verification_test: Open the batch timeline; confirm interventions, particle spikes, EM positives and alarms are displayed on one time axis and exportable.

requirement: Sterile manufacture takes place in cleanrooms entered via change rooms acting as personnel airlocks and via material airlocks, supplied with suitably filtered air and kept to the right cleanliness standard; scientifically justified controls and monitoring evaluate the state of cleanrooms, airlocks and pass-through hatches.
system_implications: The batch's EM scope must include the airlocks, change rooms and pass-through hatches actually used for personnel and material entry (derived from gowning and transfer records), not only the processing rooms.
verification_test: Transfer material through pass-through PT-2 during the batch; confirm PT-2 monitoring data appear in the batch EM summary.

requirement: Cleaning ahead of barrier-system bio-decontamination is declared essential, because leftover residues can defeat the decontamination.
system_implications: Hard sequence rule: an isolator/RABS bio-decontamination cycle is accepted as valid for the batch only if a completed cleaning record for the same enclosure precedes it with no intervening use.
verification_test: Record a VHP cycle with no prior cleaning record; confirm the cycle is marked invalid for batch use.

requirement: Visual inspection is declared not acceptable as a container-closure integrity test method.
system_implications: The CCI method list excludes visual inspection; a 100 percent visual inspection record can never satisfy a CCI requirement in master data or at release.
verification_test: Attempt to map the 100 percent visual inspection step as the CCI evidence for an ampoule product; confirm refusal.

requirement: For closed systems in aseptic processing, keeping every product-contact surface sterile is declared critical.
system_implications: Every product-contact element of an aseptic closed system (bags, tubing, connectors, sensors, filters) must resolve to a sterilisation record or supplier sterility proof before the system is released for use; no element may be 'not applicable'.
verification_test: Build a closed assembly where one connector has no sterility evidence; confirm the assembly cannot be released for use.

requirement: A passing sterility test is declared incapable of assuring sterility for a product that did not meet its design, procedural or validation parameters.
system_implications: Release logic hard rule: sterility-test results are evaluated only after all process, procedural and validation-status checks pass; a pass never closes or overrides an open nonconformance.
verification_test: Enter a passing sterility result for a batch with an unresolved sterilisation-cycle deviation; confirm status remains 'not releasable'.

requirement: Operations must take place in specifically defined areas of adequate size, using separate or defined areas, or other control systems, that prevent contamination and mixups during: receipt, identification, storage and withholding of components, containers, closures and labeling until the QCU has sampled, tested or examined and released them; holding of rejected materials pending disposition; storage of released materials; storage of in-process materials; manufacturing and processing; packaging and labeling; quarantine of drug products before release; storage of released drug products; and control and laboratory work. Buildings need space for orderly placement of equipment and materials, and material and product flows must be designed to prevent contamination and mixups.
system_implications: Room/area master data with a type (e.g., quarantine store, rejected cage, dispensing booth, compression suite, packaging hall, aseptic core) and the activities and material statuses allowed there. Each MBR step is bound to permitted area types, and execution is blocked in an area not approved for that step. Where the firm relies on 'other control systems' instead of physical segregation (e.g., electronic quarantine inside a shared warehouse), the status/location control must be validated as equally effective: quarantined or rejected stock cannot be picked, issued or dispensed, and physical labels show the same status as the system. Moves of materials, intermediates and finished product between locations are recorded with time and user.
verification_test: Execute a dispensing step from a terminal bound to a room not approved for dispensing -> blocked. Pick a quarantined lot stored in an electronically segregated shared location -> blocked. Move a rejected lot into a released-stock location type -> blocked and logged.

requirement: Ventilation must be adequate, and where appropriate for the operation there must be equipment giving adequate control of air pressure, microorganisms, dust, humidity and temperature. Air filtration (prefilters and particulate filters) is used where appropriate on air supplied to production areas; if air is recirculated, measures must control recirculation of production dust; and areas where air is contaminated during production need adequate exhaust or equivalent control systems.
system_implications: The MBR can state required room conditions per step (e.g., temperature and relative humidity ranges for moisture-sensitive granulation, compression or coating; pressure cascade and running dust extraction for potent or sensitizing compounds). At step start and during execution the eBMR reads room status or BMS/EMS values; if a limit is breached the step is blocked or a deviation is raised, per MBR rules, and the readings for the step window are attached to the batch record.
verification_test: Simulate relative humidity above the MBR limit before a humidity-sensitive step -> start blocked or deviation required per configuration. Simulate a pressure-cascade alarm during potent-compound dispensing -> deviation created and linked to the batch. The batch report shows the environmental readings for each conditioned step.

requirement: Penicillin must be manufactured, processed and packed in facilities, and with air-handling systems, completely separate from those used for other human drug products. If there is a reasonable possibility that a non-penicillin product was exposed to penicillin cross-contamination, that product must be tested for penicillin by the method incorporated by reference, and it may not be marketed if detectable levels are found.
system_implications: Product and material master data carry a penicillin flag; scheduling and batch-record issuance prevent penicillin products or components from being assigned to non-penicillin facilities, rooms or equipment, and vice versa. If an event creates a reasonable possibility of penicillin exposure (e.g., a spill in a shared warehouse or a misrouted material), QA can put the affected non-penicillin lots on hold, and the release gate then requires a penicillin test result showing none detected.
verification_test: Issue a batch record for a penicillin product in a non-penicillin facility -> blocked. Flag a non-penicillin lot as potentially exposed -> release blocked until a penicillin test result showing none detected is attached.

requirement: Buildings used to make, process, pack or hold drug products must be clean, sanitary, free of vermin (laboratory animals excepted) and in good repair, with trash and organic waste removed promptly and hygienically. Written, followed procedures must assign responsibility for sanitation and describe cleaning schedules, methods, equipment and materials in enough detail. Further written, followed procedures govern the use of suitable rodenticides, insecticides, fungicides, fumigants and cleaning or sanitizing agents so that equipment, materials and product are not contaminated; pesticides may be used only if registered and used under FIFRA. These procedures also apply to contractors and temporary staff.
system_implications: Room master data holds a cleaning/sanitation status and schedule (with cleaning agent lot and performer) and a maintenance/out-of-service status. The pre-start or line-clearance step checks that room cleaning is current and the room is not under maintenance; otherwise the step is blocked. Room cleaning by contractors or temporary staff uses the same electronic procedure and qualification checks as for employees, and cleaning agents are chosen from an approved list.
verification_test: Start a batch in a room whose scheduled cleaning is overdue -> blocked. Put a room into maintenance status -> no step can start there. A contractor without the cleaning-procedure qualification cannot sign a room-cleaning record.

requirement: Equipment surfaces that touch components, in-process materials or product must not react with, add to or absorb from them to a degree that moves the product's safety, identity, strength, quality or purity outside official or established requirements. Substances needed to run equipment, such as lubricants or coolants, must not contact components, containers, closures, in-process materials or product in a way that does so.
system_implications: Equipment master data carries a qualification status (including review of product-contact materials), and only qualified equipment can be selected for a step. Where equipment uses lubricants or coolants that could reach product, the approved grade is recorded in maintenance records, and a leak or contact event observed during a batch forces a deviation linked to that batch.
verification_test: Select equipment whose qualification is expired or pending -> blocked. Record a lubricant-leak event on a running step -> deviation created and batch flagged for QA review.

requirement: Detailed written, followed procedures must cover how components, containers and closures are received, identified, stored, handled, sampled, tested, and approved or rejected. Each container or group of containers of these materials must carry a distinctive code for every lot of every shipment received; the code is then used when recording the lot's disposition, and each lot's status (quarantined, approved or rejected) must be identified.
system_implications: At receipt the system assigns a unique receiving/control code per lot per shipment (two deliveries of the same supplier lot get different codes), prints container labels bearing that code and the status, and uses the code as the key in disposition, dispensing and genealogy records. Status on screen and on physical labels must match, so a status change triggers relabelling or label re-validation.
verification_test: Receive the same supplier lot in two shipments -> two distinct receiving codes. Change status to Approved -> the label and status display update and dispensing scans read the new status. Attempt a disposition without the receiving code -> not possible.

requirement: On arrival and before acceptance, each container or group of containers of components, containers and closures is visually examined for correct content labeling, container damage or broken seals, and contamination. The materials then stay in quarantine until tested or examined, as appropriate, and released, with storage meeting 211.80.
system_implications: The receiving transaction includes a mandatory visual examination per container group (labeling against the order and material master, damage, seal integrity, contamination) with the examiner's identity; failures route to rejection or QA assessment. Received lots default to Quarantine and cannot be allocated, picked or dispensed until QCU release. Examination results form part of the 211.184(b) record.
verification_test: Complete a receipt without the visual examination -> not possible. Record a broken seal -> lot routed to QA hold. Try to dispense a newly received lot -> blocked (Quarantine).

requirement: Representative samples must be taken from each shipment of each lot of components, containers and closures; the number of containers sampled and the amount taken per container are based on sound criteria such as statistics on variability, confidence and precision, the supplier's quality history, and the quantity needed for analysis and for 211.170 reserve samples. Sampling must: clean container exteriors where needed so the material is not contaminated; open, sample and reseal containers without contaminating their contents or other materials; use sterile equipment and aseptic technique when needed; not composite top, middle and bottom sub-samples when such stratified sampling is required; label sample containers so the material, lot, source container, sampling date and sampler can be determined; and mark sampled containers to show samples were removed.
system_implications: If sampling runs through the eBMR/WMS: the sampling plan (number of containers and quantity per material and supplier status) is master data; the system selects or confirms the containers to sample, prints sample labels showing material, lot, source container ID, date and sampler, marks the sampled containers electronically and on the label, and records the quantity taken (including reserve quantity for active ingredients). For sterile-product components the plan can require aseptic sampling (booth, sterile tools) and records it. Stratified sub-samples are labelled individually and cannot be merged in the system.
verification_test: Sample a lot -> labels carry all five identification elements and source containers show a sampled mark. Sample fewer containers than the plan requires -> blocked or deviation. Merge top/middle/bottom sub-samples where stratified sampling is required -> blocked.

requirement: Each component must get at least one identity test (a specific one where it exists) and be tested for conformity with its written purity, strength and quality specifications; instead of full in-house testing, a supplier's report of analysis may be accepted if the manufacturer runs at least one specific identity test and establishes, and re-checks at appropriate intervals, the reliability of the supplier's results. Containers and closures are tested against their written specifications, or a supplier's certificate of testing is accepted provided the manufacturer does at least a visual identification and periodically validates the supplier's results. Components are examined microscopically when appropriate; lots liable to filth, insect infestation or other extraneous adulterants are examined against specifications for them; and lots with potential for objectionable microbial contamination, given their use, are micro-tested before use. Lots meeting the specifications may be approved and released; others are rejected.
system_implications: The QCU release transaction for a component, container or closure lot requires, according to material master settings: an identity result (always for components), full-test or CoA-reliance results, and microbial, filth or microscopic results where flagged. CoA reliance is selectable only while the supplier/material pair has a current supplier-results validation status; when that lapses the material reverts to full testing. For injectables, components with objectionable-microbe risk (e.g., certain excipients and closures) carry mandatory microbial test flags as the firm defines them.
verification_test: Release a component lot on a CoA alone without an in-house identity test -> blocked. Let the supplier validation status lapse -> CoA-based release no longer offered. Release a container lot on a certificate with no visual identification record -> blocked.

requirement: Approved components, drug product containers and closures must be used in rotation so that the oldest approved stock goes first; temporary and appropriate departures from this are allowed.
system_implications: Dispensing and line-side issue propose the oldest approved lot first (by approval date, or by a documented equivalent such as earliest retest/expiry where the SOP justifies it). Choosing another lot requires a recorded reason, reportable so that departures can be shown to be temporary and appropriate.
verification_test: With two approved lots available, the system proposes the older one; picking the newer one requires a reason, which appears in a rotation-exception report.

requirement: Drug product containers and closures must not react with, add to or absorb from the drug to a degree that changes its safety, identity, strength, quality or purity beyond official or established requirements, and the container-closure system must adequately protect the product against foreseeable external factors during storage and use that could cause deterioration or contamination.
system_implications: These are design and qualification requirements; the eBMR enforces them by allowing only the container-closure components specified in the approved master record (item code and approved grade/supplier) to be issued and scanned at filling or packaging, with substitutions requiring change control. For injectables, the container-closure checks defined in the MBR (e.g., capping/crimp checks) are executed and recorded.
verification_test: Scan a closure item code not in the MBR bill of materials -> blocked. Try to approve an MBR whose container-closure components are not qualified in master data -> approval blocked.

requirement: Written, followed warehousing procedures must provide for holding drug products in quarantine until the QCU releases them, and for storing drug products under temperature, humidity and light conditions that keep their identity, strength, quality and purity unaffected.
system_implications: Finished lots are created in Quarantine status and become shippable only through the QCU disposition signature; any movement before release is flagged as under quarantine. Product master data holds storage conditions (from labeling and stability data); the eBMR records conditions for bulk, intermediate and finished-product holds within the batch (e.g., cold-chain holds for injectables, light protection) and links warehouse excursion events to affected lots so QA can assess them and, where needed, trigger re-evaluation or a 211.192 investigation.
verification_test: Try to ship a finished lot in Quarantine -> blocked in the integrated WMS/ERP. Inject a temperature excursion for a storage location -> the affected lots are listed and flagged for QA assessment.

requirement: Laboratory controls must include scientifically sound specifications, standards, sampling plans and test procedures, and must determine conformance: for each lot within each shipment of components, containers, closures and labeling (with written descriptions of sampling and testing, and retesting of materials that can deteriorate); for in-process materials; and for drug products. In every case the samples must be representative and properly identified. Sampling and testing plans for drug products must state the sampling method and how many units per batch are tested, and must be followed.
system_implications: Every sample drawn during eBMR execution (in-process, finished product, stability, reserve) is created from an MBR-defined sampling plan (point, method, number of units or quantity), receives a unique sample ID and label (product, lot, sampling point, date/time, sampler), and is sent to LIMS with that identity. The system checks the quantity or unit count against the plan, records any departure as a deviation, and prevents results from being attached to a sample from a different lot.
verification_test: Take fewer units than the plan specifies -> deviation required. LIMS receives the sample with the correct lot and sampling point. Attach a result to a sample from another lot -> rejected.

requirement: Instruments, apparatus, gauges and recording devices must be calibrated at suitable intervals under an established written program that gives specific directions, schedules, limits for accuracy and precision, and remedial action when those limits are not met; devices that do not meet their specifications must not be used. Complete records of this periodic calibration must be kept.
system_implications: Every measuring device used in eBMR steps (balances, pH meters, thermometers, pressure gauges, checkweighers, filter integrity testers, chart recorders) is in the instrument master with its calibration schedule, accuracy/precision limits and status, and use is blocked when calibration is overdue or failed. When an as-found calibration fails, the system lists every batch and step measured with that device since its last passing calibration so QA can carry out the remedial impact assessment, which is linked to the calibration record.
verification_test: Record a failed as-found calibration for a balance -> the system lists the affected batches since the last passing calibration and blocks the balance until it is recalibrated. Calibration records are retrievable from each batch that used the device.

requirement: Complete records must be kept of any modification of an established test method, giving the reason and data showing that the modified method is at least as accurate and reliable for the material tested; and complete records must show how laboratory reference standards, reagents and standard solutions were tested and standardized.
system_implications: For tests executed in the eBMR, the method is fixed by the MBR version; any modification goes through change control with justification and comparative data before the MBR can use it, and during execution a method cannot be altered ad hoc (only a documented deviation is possible). Reagents and standard solutions used in shop-floor tests (e.g., pH calibration buffers, titrants, reference standards) are scanned by lot, checked for expiry and standardization status, and recorded with the result.
verification_test: Run a test using an expired pH buffer lot -> blocked. Change a test-method parameter in an Effective MBR without change control -> not possible.

requirement: A written, followed stability program must assess product stability, and its results are used to set storage conditions and expiration dates. It includes statistically based sample sizes and test intervals, storage conditions for retained samples, reliable and specific methods, testing in the marketed container-closure system, and, for products reconstituted at dispensing, testing both as dispensed and after reconstitution. Enough batches must be tested to set an appropriate expiration date, with the data kept; accelerated data may support a tentative date only while full shelf-life studies continue until that date is confirmed or corrected. Complete records of all stability testing are kept.
system_implications: The eBMR records stability samples drawn from a batch (quantity, marketed container-closure, storage condition, study ID) as sampling events linked to the stability study in LIMS. Expiry dates used in a batch come only from product master data whose shelf life references approved stability data; a tentative, accelerated-data-based shelf life is flagged so batches made under it can be found if the date later changes.
verification_test: Enroll a batch in a stability study -> the sampling event, quantity and container-closure appear in the BPR and LIMS. Change shelf life in the product master without a stability-data reference -> blocked. Query all batches labelled under a tentative expiry -> correct set returned.

clause: 211.167(c) (211.167(b), ophthalmic ointments, is outside the tablets/injectables scope)
requirement: Each batch of a controlled-release dosage form must undergo appropriate laboratory testing showing it meets the specification for the release rate of each active ingredient, using written test procedures that are followed.
system_implications: Product master data flags modified/controlled-release products; for them the release gate requires an in-specification drug-release (dissolution) result for every active ingredient before QA can sign release.
verification_test: For an extended-release tablet lot with one active ingredient's release-rate result missing -> release blocked; with all results in specification -> release allowed.

requirement: For each lot in each shipment of each active ingredient, an appropriately identified, representative reserve sample must be kept, of at least twice the amount needed for all tests that determine whether it meets its specifications, excluding sterility and pyrogen tests. It is kept until 1 year past the expiry of the last drug product lot that contains that active ingredient; for radioactive products (other than nonradioactive reagent kits), 3 or 6 months after that expiry depending on whether the dating period is 30 days or less or longer; and for OTC products exempt from expiry dating, 3 years after distribution of the last lot containing it.
system_implications: At receipt or sampling of an active-ingredient lot the system requires a reserve-sample record (quantity checked against twice the specification test quantity from the test plan, excluding sterility/pyrogen tests; storage location). The reserve's retention end date is recalculated from genealogy as later finished lots use that API lot, and disposal before that date is blocked.
verification_test: Receive an API lot and try to complete sampling without a reserve sample of sufficient quantity -> blocked. Use the API lot in a new batch with a later expiry -> the reserve retention date moves out accordingly; disposal before it -> blocked.

requirement: For each lot or batch of drug product, an appropriately identified, representative reserve sample must be kept under conditions consistent with the labeling, in the same immediate container-closure system as the marketed product (or one with essentially the same characteristics), of at least twice the amount needed for all required tests except sterility and pyrogen tests. Except for radioactive products, reserve samples from representative lots chosen by acceptable statistical procedures are visually examined at least once a year for signs of deterioration, unless examination would compromise the sample; any deterioration is investigated under 211.192, and results are recorded with the product's other stability data. Retention is 1 year after the product's expiration date, with shorter periods for radioactive products and 3 years after distribution for OTC products exempt from expiry dating.
system_implications: The filling or packaging MBR contains a reserve-sample step: quantity computed as at least twice the release-test quantity (excluding sterility/pyrogen tests), taken in the marketed immediate container-closure, labelled and moved to a reserve location stored per labeling. Reserve units are included in yield and label reconciliation. The system schedules the annual visual examination for statistically selected lots, records results, opens an investigation on deterioration, and blocks disposal before the retention end date.
verification_test: Complete packaging without the reserve-sample step, or with less than the computed quantity -> blocked. The annual examination list is generated and a recorded deterioration opens an investigation. Dispose of a reserve before 1 year past expiry -> blocked.

requirement: Procedures must make sure the firm's responsible officials, if they are not personally involved or already aware, are told in writing about investigations under 211.198 (complaints), 211.204 (returns) or 211.208 (salvage), about recalls, about FDA inspection-observation reports, and about any FDA regulatory action relating to good manufacturing practice.
system_implications: Usually a QMS function. Where the eBMR hosts or links investigations, opening a complaint-, return- or salvage-related investigation, or linking a recall to a lot, triggers a written notification to the configured responsible officials with acknowledgement tracking, and the notification record is linked to the lots concerned.
verification_test: Open a return-related investigation for a lot -> the configured officials receive a notification, and the notification with its timestamp appears in the investigation record.

requirement: Returned drug products must be identified as returns and held. If the conditions under which they were held, stored or shipped before or during return, or the state of the product, container, carton or labeling, cast doubt on their safety, identity, strength, quality or purity, they must be destroyed unless examination, testing or other investigation shows they meet appropriate standards; reprocessing is allowed if the result meets appropriate standards, specifications and characteristics. Return records must show the product name and label potency of the dosage form, the lot (or control or batch) number, the reason for return, the quantity returned, the date of disposition and the final disposition. If the reason for return implicates associated batches, a 211.192 investigation is required. Holding, testing and reprocessing of returns follow written procedures.
system_implications: Returns are received against the original lot (genealogy link) into a Returned/Hold status that blocks redistribution. The return record captures the mandatory fields (product and label potency, lot, reason, quantity, disposition date, final disposition) plus evidence on storage and shipping conditions. Disposition is QCU-only: destroy, return to stock only with documented examination or test evidence, or reprocess through the reprocessing path (US-211-115). A reason code that implicates other batches forces a linked 211.192 investigation, and return data feed the annual product review.
verification_test: Receive a return without a reason -> not possible. Return a lot to saleable stock without examination or test evidence -> blocked. Choose a reason code flagged as batch-related -> an investigation is created and linked to the original batch record.

requirement: Drug products exposed to improper storage conditions (extreme temperature, humidity, smoke, fumes, pressure, age or radiation) because of natural disasters, fires, accidents or equipment failures must not be salvaged and put back on the market. Where it is unclear whether products were so exposed, salvaging is allowed only with laboratory test and assay evidence (including animal feeding studies where applicable) that the products meet all applicable identity, strength, quality and purity standards, and with evidence from inspection of the premises that the products and their packaging were not exposed to improper conditions; organoleptic examination counts only as supplementary evidence. Records including name, lot number and disposition are kept.
system_implications: QA can place all lots in an affected location or time window on a Salvage-Hold status (selected through location and genealogy queries), blocking distribution. Any 'salvage' disposition requires both linked laboratory evidence and a premises-inspection record; a disposition supported only by organoleptic checks is refused. Records capture product name, lot and disposition, and salvage events feed the annual review and responsible-official notification (211.180(e)-(f)).
verification_test: Place a warehouse zone on salvage hold -> all lots in it are blocked. Try to release a salvage-hold lot with only an organoleptic record -> blocked. With lab evidence and a premises-inspection record, QA can release and the record shows name, lot and disposition.

requirement: Electronic signatures, with their records, that meet Part 11 are treated as equivalent to full handwritten signatures, initials and other signings required by FDA regulations, unless a regulation effective on or after 20 August 1997 specifically excludes them; compliant electronic records may be used instead of paper unless paper is specifically required. A handwritten signature applied to an electronic record (e.g., a name or mark written with a stylus on a device that captures it) is a handwritten signature, not an electronic signature, and must still satisfy 11.50 and 11.70.
system_implications: Wherever Part 211 calls for a signature or initials (e.g., full handwritten signature on the master record in 211.186(a), sign or initial in 211.182, tester and reviewer initials or signature in 211.194(a)(7)-(8), dated approval signature on labeling specimens in 211.186(b)(8)), the eBMR uses a full Part 11 e-signature (11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200, 11.300), not a lighter acknowledge click. If stylus/handwritten capture is offered, it must show printed name, date/time and meaning and be bound to the record. The URS should inventory every predicate-rule signature point and the signature type used for it.
verification_test: Review the signature-point inventory: every Part 211 signature or initials requirement maps to a Part 11-compliant signature event. Try to complete a 211.182 cleaning-log entry with a non-signature acknowledgement -> not possible.

requirement: Anyone using a closed system to create, modify, maintain or transmit electronic records must apply procedures and controls designed to protect the records' authenticity and integrity, their confidentiality where appropriate, and to ensure a signer cannot readily repudiate a signed record as not genuine; paragraphs (a) to (k) list the minimum controls.
system_implications: Beyond the (a)-(k) controls: decide which eBMR data need confidentiality (e.g., proprietary formulas, personal data of operators, health-related exclusion notes) and restrict read access by role and site, with encryption in transit and at rest as a design choice; support non-repudiation by keeping an evidence package per signature (identity-verification record, authentication event, signature manifestation, audit trail) so a signer cannot credibly deny it.
verification_test: A user without formula-view permission cannot read the MBR composition. For a sampled signature, the system produces the identity-verification record, authentication event and audit trail tying it to the signer.

clause: Ch.4 preamble 'Required GMP documentation' - Records (raw data)
requirement: Records include the raw data from which other records are generated. For electronic records the regulated user must define which data count as raw data, and as a minimum every data item on which a quality decision is based must be defined as raw data.
system_implications: Maintain a raw-data classification per master and per data field (e.g., raw / derived / informational) under change control; as a minimum, every value feeding a quality decision (weights, IPC results, CPP readings, yields, reconciliation counts, alarms used in review-by-exception, EM results used for release) is raw data. Raw data are retained unaltered with metadata and audit trail for the batch retention period, including data captured from PLC/SCADA, historians and instruments that the eBMR only summarises (compliance summaries under the 4.20 Note must not replace them). Derived values keep their inputs and the calculation version.
verification_test: Inspect the raw-data register for one tablet and one injectable master: every field used in an IPC, yield/reconciliation or release decision is classified raw. For a summarised parameter (e.g., fill weight trend or compression force), retrieve the underlying raw data for the batch. Recompute a derived value from its stored inputs and confirm it matches.

clause: Ch.4 preamble 'Required GMP documentation' - instruction type (manufacturing formulae, processing, packaging and testing instructions)
requirement: Manufacturing formulae and processing, packaging and testing instructions must spell out every starting material, item of equipment and computerised system (if any) to be used, and give complete instructions for processing, packaging, sampling and testing; where relevant they must also name the in-process controls and process analytical technology (PAT) to be applied, with acceptance criteria.
system_implications: Each master step names the computerised systems it relies on (e.g., the eBMR itself, PLC/SCADA recipe and version, weighing system, checkweigher, vision/serialisation system, autoclave or lyophiliser controller, filter-integrity tester), so the batch record shows which validated system and version produced the data. Where PAT is used (e.g., NIR blend uniformity for tablets, in-line checks on injectable lines), the master defines the PAT method, model version and acceptance criteria and the record captures the result against them. Sampling steps carry their sampling instructions.
verification_test: Review a master: every step using an automated system names that system and its approved version/recipe; a PAT step without acceptance criteria cannot be approved; executing a batch records the system/recipe version actually used and flags any mismatch with the master.

requirement: Instructions must be error-free and must be available in written, human-readable form.
system_implications: Before a master is approved its content is independently verified (quantities and units, limits, calculation formulas, equipment classes, step order), ideally supported by automated consistency checks (BOM total against batch size, units consistent, limits within registered ranges). Operators can always see the current instruction text at each step, including during downtime via the Annex 11 §16 fallback (printable instructions generated from the effective master).
verification_test: Seed a draft master with a unit error and a limit outside the registered range: the automated checks or the verification step catch both before approval. Confirm each executing step displays its instruction text and that a printable version is available in downtime mode.

clause: Ch.4 preamble 'Required GMP documentation' - Certificates of Analysis, footnote 1
requirement: Where the marketing authorisation provides for it (real-time release testing), certification can be based fully or partly on evaluating summaries and exception reports of real-time batch data from PAT or from process parameters and metrics, instead of end-product test results.
system_implications: Conditional - only if RTRT/PAT-based release is in the MA: the eBMR generates, per batch, a validated summary and exception report of the PAT/parameter data the MA specifies, linked to the MA reference and model version, available to the QP for certification, with the underlying raw data retained (EUA-NEW-01). Not applicable otherwise.
verification_test: For an RTRT product, run a batch with one PAT excursion: the summary shows compliance per registered attribute, the excursion appears in the exception report and is visible to the QP before certification, and the underlying spectra/parameter data are retrievable.

requirement: Approved, dated specifications must exist for starting materials, packaging materials and finished products, and specifications for intermediate and bulk products must be available for critical steps or when such products are bought in or dispatched. Material specifications include how materials are stored and how long they can be held before re-testing; finished-product specifications include the formula, dosage form and pack, storage and handling needs, and shelf-life.
system_implications: Master data reference the current approved specification version for the product (4.17(a)) and for each packaging component (4.19(d)); a new specification version triggers an impact assessment on the masters. At dispensing the eBMR checks the lot is released and within its re-test or expiry date (enforcement itself is Ch.5 5.34, see EU5-27). Hold points at critical steps, and bulk dispatched to another site (e.g., bulk tablets to a packager, bulk solution to a filling site), apply the approved intermediate/bulk specification limits. The expiry date recorded and printed on packs is calculated from the shelf-life in the effective finished-product specification using a defined start-of-shelf-life rule.
verification_test: Try to dispense a lot past its re-test date - blocked. In a test system change the finished-product shelf-life and confirm new batches use the new value only once the specification is effective. Dispatch a bulk batch and confirm its record shows results against the approved bulk specification.

requirement: Every incoming delivery - starting materials of any kind (bulk, intermediates and finished goods included) and all primary, secondary and printed packaging materials - must be received under a written procedure and recorded. Receipt records must let each received lot be identified (external and internal names or codes, supplier and manufacturer with the manufacturer's batch number, and the internal batch number assigned on receipt) and quantified (total quantity, number of containers and date received), with room for relevant remarks.
system_implications: Where the eBMR/MES suite handles goods receipt it captures these data and assigns the internal lot number. In all cases the lot scanned at dispensing or at packaging-material issue must resolve to its receipt record (supplier, manufacturer and manufacturer's batch), giving genealogy from supplier lot to finished batch for traceability (4.8) and recall. Bulk or intermediates received from another site are received like starting materials.
verification_test: From a finished batch, trace an API lot and a printed carton lot back to receipt records showing manufacturer and manufacturer's batch number. Attempt to issue a lot that has no receipt record - blocked.

requirement: Written procedures must govern how starting materials, packaging materials and, as appropriate, other materials are labelled internally, held in quarantine and stored.
system_implications: Labels the eBMR prints for dispensed materials, intermediates and bulk containers (content, lot, quantity, status, hold/expiry date, storage condition) follow approved, version-controlled templates defined under that procedure. The eBMR displays and respects material status (quarantine, released, rejected) and prevents use of quarantined or rejected material (the use prohibition itself is Ch.5); status changes are e-signed and audit-trailed.
verification_test: Print a dispensing label and an intermediate container label and confirm template version and mandatory fields. Try to use a quarantined intermediate in a following step - blocked. Release it with a QA e-signature and confirm the step can then proceed.

requirement: Sampling must follow written procedures that set the method, equipment and amount to take and the precautions against contaminating or degrading the material; testing of materials and products at the different manufacturing stages must follow written procedures describing methods and equipment, and the tests performed must be recorded; and clear operating procedures must be available for major manufacturing and test equipment.
system_implications: Sampling and IPC steps reference the governing procedure and version and show the amount to take, sampling tool and precautions (aseptic sampling precautions for sterile products); sample IDs and quantities withdrawn are recorded so they enter yield and reconciliation. Every test performed in production (IPC or at-line) is recorded with result, method reference and performer, including repeat tests, which are added as new results rather than overwriting. Steps operating major equipment link to the current effective operating procedure.
verification_test: Execute a sampling step: the record shows procedure/version, sample ID, quantity taken and sampler. Repeat an IPC test: both results are visible. The equipment procedure link opens the current effective version.

requirement: Written procedures and associated records are required for personnel matters, including signature lists, GMP and technical training (and checks that it was effective), and gowning and hygiene; Annex 11 §2 requires personnel to have appropriate qualifications for their assigned duties.
system_implications: Maintain an electronic signature register linking each user ID to full name, initials if used, roles, permitted signature types and validity dates, retained as long as any record that user signed. Integrate training records so users can perform or verify only steps for which their training is current (training gating is good practice rather than an explicit Ch.4 rule). For injectables, aseptic-area steps can require current gowning qualification.
verification_test: Resolve any signer on an archived batch record to full name and role valid on the signing date. Expire a user's training for a step and confirm the system blocks that user from performing it, with the block audit-trailed.

clause: Ch.4 4.29 (validation and qualification, change control, deviations and non-conformances, complaints, recalls, returns, record summaries such as product quality review); 4.27
requirement: Policies, procedures, protocols, reports and records of actions or conclusions are required for quality processes that touch batches - among them validation and qualification, change control, investigation of deviations and non-conformances, complaints, recalls and returns - and for record summaries where appropriate, such as the product quality review.
system_implications: Each batch record links to the deviations/investigations raised on it, to the change control behind its master version, and to later complaints, returns or recalls involving it; master versions reference their change-control record and supporting validation; batches made under a validation or study protocol are flagged and linked to that protocol. Provide a structured export of batch data for product quality review (yields, IPC trends, deviations, reconciliation results, changes) so PQR summaries are drawn from source records rather than re-keyed.
verification_test: From a batch, open its linked deviations and the change control of its master version; from a complaint, find the batch record. Export PQR data for a product over a period and reconcile totals against the individual batch records.

clause: Ch.4 4.29 (environmental monitoring); 4.27 (all records available to the QP)
requirement: Written procedures and records are required for environmental monitoring, and every record relevant to a batch must be available to the QP.
system_implications: Injectables: the batch record links the environmental and personnel monitoring results for the rooms/Grade A zones and time window of aseptic processing and shows open excursions to the QP before certification (batch-linked EM review detail comes from Annex 1, beyond Ch.4). Tablets: EM records may stay outside the eBMR, but rooms and times used must be traceable so the relevant EM data can be retrieved.
verification_test: For an aseptic fill, open the batch review and confirm the EM results for the filling room and time window are linked, and that an open EM excursion is flagged on the QP screen.

requirement: The quality management system must keep a maintained list (inventory) of its documents.
system_implications: The eBMR can list all its controlled documents - processing and packaging masters, templates, forms, label templates, embedded work instructions - with ID, version, status, effective date and next review date, for inclusion in or synchronisation with the site document inventory.
verification_test: Generate the list and reconcile it with the site document inventory: every effective master/template appears once, with matching version and status.

requirement: Validation documentation and reports must cover the relevant steps of the system life cycle, and the manufacturer must be able to defend, from its risk assessment, the validation approach it chose - the standards and protocols used, the acceptance criteria, and the procedures and records produced.
system_implications: The eBMR validation package spans the life cycle from requirements through operation to retirement, including configuration of master/recipe types, interfaces, calculations, reports and data migration, with a documented risk rationale for test depth; new masters and configuration changes are verified under the same approach. Plan retirement (data retention and readability after decommissioning) as part of the life cycle.
verification_test: Review the validation plan and report: they cover requirements through operation and retirement, cite the risk assessment for test depth, and include verification of a sample of configured masters.

requirement: Manufacturing must be carried out to clearly defined procedures and in line with GMP so that products reach the required quality, and it must match what the site's manufacturing authorisation and the product's marketing authorisation (MA) allow.
system_implications: Master recipes and packaging instructions carry the MA reference (product, MA number, market) and the registered data they must respect (formula, batch size or range, registered process parameters and IPC limits, specifications, shelf life). Master approval includes a documented regulatory-conformity sign-off; a master cannot set limits wider than the registered values without a linked regulatory-variation reference; batches can only be created from an approved, effective master version valid for the target market. DESIGN CHOICES: the approval roles, the hard block on registered ranges, and sourcing MA data from a regulatory information system by interface.
verification_test: Try to approve a master revision whose CPP range is wider than the registered range with no variation reference -> blocked. Create a batch for a market not linked to the master's MA -> refused. The batch record shows the master version and MA reference used.

requirement: Every incoming consignment must be checked to confirm it matches the order, and containers are cleaned where needed and labelled with the prescribed information. For each delivery of starting material, every container is checked for package integrity (including any tamper-evident seal) and the delivery note, purchase order and supplier labels are checked against each other and against the manufacturer's own approved manufacturer/supplier records; these receiving checks are documented.
system_implications: If the MES/WMS performs goods receipt: a receipt transaction records the order match, a per-container integrity/seal check and any cleaning, compares the manufacturer and supplier shown on the delivery documents/labels with the approved-source master data (mismatch -> lot blocked and routed to QC; see EUB-NEW-09), prints receipt labels with the prescribed data, and signs off the documented checks. If receipt is done in ERP/WMS: the eBMR accepts for dispensing/issue only lots whose receipt checks are flagged complete through the interface. DESIGN CHOICES: the automatic comparison and the blocking.
verification_test: Receive a lot whose supplier label names a manufacturer not on the approved list -> lot blocked for QC. Try to dispense from a lot whose receipt checks are not recorded as complete -> refused. The receipt record shows each check with user and time.

requirement: Any damage to containers, or any other problem that could harm a material's quality, must be investigated, recorded and reported to the QC department.
system_implications: At receipt, storage, dispensing and charging, users can raise a 'material/container problem' record against the specific container (damaged or leaking container, broken seal, signs of contamination, abnormal appearance); QC is notified automatically and the investigation outcome is recorded against the lot. DESIGN CHOICE: automatic hold of the container (optionally the whole lot) until QC records a disposition.
verification_test: During dispensing, report a damaged drum -> record created, QC notified, container blocked; attempt to dispense from it before QC disposition -> refused; the QC disposition and investigation appear in the lot history.

requirement: Bought-in intermediates and bulk products are to be treated at receipt exactly like starting materials.
system_implications: Purchased intermediates/bulk (e.g. bought-in bulk tablets for packaging; a bought-in intermediate or bulk solution for filling) go through the starting-material flow: quarantine on receipt, receipt checks, sampling/identity testing, QC release, identity labelling and approved-source check before they can be issued to a processing or packaging order; the genealogy links the external lot and its manufacturer batch number to the finished batch.
verification_test: Issue a purchased bulk lot still in quarantine to a packaging order -> refused. After QC release it can be issued and appears in the genealogy with the supplier's batch number.

requirement: All materials and products must be kept under the storage conditions the manufacturer has defined, and stored in an orderly way that allows batches to be kept apart and stock to be rotated.
system_implications: The material/product master holds storage conditions; storage, staging and line-side locations managed by the MES carry condition attributes, and the system prevents placing a lot in a location with incompatible conditions (e.g. 2-8 C material in ambient staging). Lot/container-level location tracking keeps batches segregated. DESIGN CHOICES: FEFO/FIFO picking proposals with a recorded reason for any override; time-out-of-storage tracking for temperature-sensitive materials.
verification_test: Try to stage a 2-8 C material in an ambient location -> blocked. Picking proposes the earliest-expiry released lot; selecting another requires a recorded reason.

requirement: Only authorised staff may enter production areas.
system_implications: Primarily a facility/physical access-control measure; the eBMR supports rather than enforces it. Support: an area-authorisation list per room/area; a user can perform or sign steps executed in a restricted area only if authorised for that area (for aseptic areas also a valid gowning qualification, which is an Annex 1 requirement); optional interface to the access-control system to cross-check that the signer was badged into the room. DESIGN CHOICES: all of these enforcement mechanisms.
verification_test: A user not authorised for the filling suite attempts to sign a filling step -> refused. After an authorisation is withdrawn, the user can no longer sign steps in that area.

clause: Ch.5 5.19; 5.21 (organisational measures on campaign cleaning, cleaning verification, cleaning records and status labels; technical measure on validated clean-in-place); with Ch.4 4.31
requirement: Cleaning processes must be effective and reproducible (5.19). Among the cross-contamination measures chosen through QRM, 5.21 lists: detailed cleaning records designed to prove cleaning was completed per the approved procedure; status labels showing the cleaning state of rooms and equipment; campaign working ended by cleaning of validated effectiveness; post-campaign cleaning verification for higher-risk products; and automatic clean-in-place of validated effectiveness. Combined with Ch.4 4.31 (logbooks recording cleaning of production equipment and areas), electronic cleaning records and cleaning-status indication are a baseline eBMR/MES function rather than an option.
system_implications: Electronic equipment/room logbook: each cleaning (manual cleaning, CIP/SIP cycles on injectable compounding/filling equipment, parts washing in common wash areas) is recorded against the equipment/room with cleaning type, procedure version, start/end and performer, and for automated cycles the cycle data and pass/fail. Equipment/room status (in use, to be cleaned, cleaned, product last processed) is derived from these records and shown on the status label/display, so nothing can show 'clean' without a completed record. Campaign counters and end-of-campaign cleaning are enforced where the QRM defines campaigns; post-campaign verification results are recorded where the QRM requires them. DESIGN CHOICES: second-person check of cleaning; clean-hold-time expiry (Annex 15 cleaning validation).
verification_test: Try to set equipment status to 'clean' without a completed cleaning record for the current procedure version -> impossible. Equipment used for product A and not cleaned cannot be allocated to product B, and its display shows 'to be cleaned - product A, batch X'. A failed CIP cycle leaves the vessel in 'to be cleaned'.

clause: Ch.5 5.21 (organisational measure on recording spills, accidental events and procedural deviations); see also 5.15, 5.22
requirement: As one of the QRM-selected organisational controls against cross-contamination, spills, accidental events and departures from procedures are to be recorded.
system_implications: An event log available from every processing and packaging step (spill, container breakage, filter/bag rupture, powder release, containment breach, equipment failure with product exposure) captures location, materials/batches affected, quantity and immediate clean-up actions; it is linked to the batch record and to the room/equipment logbook, and the affected room/equipment is set to 'cleaning required'. Events that are departures from procedure feed the deviation process (5.15), and all events feed the periodic review of cross-contamination measures (5.22). DESIGN CHOICE: blocking further steps in the room until cleaning is recorded.
verification_test: Log a powder spill in the granulation suite -> event appears in the batch record and exception report, room status changes to 'cleaning required', and (if configured) the next step in that room is blocked until cleaning is recorded. The periodic review report lists the event.

requirement: Choosing, qualifying, approving and maintaining suppliers of starting materials, and of primary and printed packaging materials, must be documented within the PQS, with oversight proportionate to each material's risk and supporting evidence kept; where possible, starting materials are bought directly from their manufacturer. For active substances, supply-chain traceability back to the active-substance starting materials must be established, its risks formally assessed and periodically verified, and the traceability records held by the EEA manufacturer or importer; API manufacturers and distributors are audited for GMP/GDP compliance at risk-based intervals. Excipients and their suppliers are controlled on the basis of a formalised risk assessment.
system_implications: Largely QMS/ERP: audits, quality agreements (5.28) and excipient risk assessments need no eBMR function. eBMR/MES support: the material master holds approved manufacturer/supplier combinations for starting and primary/printed packaging materials with their approval status, and lots from unapproved or suspended sources are blocked at receipt and at dispensing/issue (interface check); batch genealogy records for every API lot its manufacturer, supplier/distributor and manufacturer batch number, so traceability from a finished batch back to the API source can be produced on demand. DESIGN CHOICE: repeating the source check at dispensing as well as at receipt.
verification_test: Suspend an API manufacturer in the approved-source list -> its lots can no longer be received or dispensed. The genealogy report for a finished batch lists each API lot with manufacturer, supplier and manufacturer batch number.

requirement: When a single delivery of a material contains several batches, each batch is to be handled on its own for sampling, testing and release.
system_implications: Receipt creates a separate internal lot for each supplier batch in the delivery; sampling plans, test results and QC status are held per lot; dispensing and genealogy reference the internal lot mapped to its supplier batch; the system does not allow one internal lot to span two supplier batches, nor a whole delivery to be released in a single action.
verification_test: Receive one delivery containing three supplier batches -> three internal lots created; releasing one leaves the other two in quarantine; an attempt to book two supplier batches into one internal lot -> refused.

clause: Q1a (whole life cycle; design for detection); binding basis 211.68(b) (input/output checked for accuracy), 211.188, 211.192
requirement: Data integrity should hold from first capture through use, storage and transfer to disposal after the retention period, and system design and controls should make errors, omissions and aberrant results easy to spot throughout (recommendation; the binding hooks are the 211.68(b) accuracy checks and the record-review duties in 211.188/211.192).
system_implications: Real-time checks against MBR limits and expected ranges; mandatory-entry and step-completeness checks before sign-off; detection of out-of-sequence or late entries; reconciliation of interface transfers (eBMR to ERP/LIMS/historian) by counts or checksums; an exception list feeding step and QA review; integrity check on archive retrieval.
verification_test: Seed a test batch with an out-of-limit value, a skipped mandatory entry, an out-of-order timestamp and a dropped interface message: each is flagged and appears in the review exception list; restoring an archived batch passes the integrity check.

clause: Q1b (audit trails count as metadata; data-metadata link secure and traceable), Q1c (audit trail scope; justification for reprocessing); binding basis 11.10(e); 211.68(b), 211.188, 211.194
requirement: Audit trails should let reviewers reconstruct how each electronic record was created, changed or deleted, covering data-level events (e.g., parameters, results) and record/system-level events (e.g., access attempts, renaming or deleting files); FDA's HPLC example expects who ran it, when, the processing settings, and any reprocessing with its reason. Audit trails are themselves metadata, to be retained with the data for the retention period with the relationship kept secure. Binding: 11.10(e) requires secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails of operator entries and actions, kept as long as the records.
system_implications: Each GMP audit entry holds user, timestamp, record and field, old and new value, action type and reason for change; a protected system log records logins and failed logins, role and permission changes, configuration changes, voids and deletion attempts; audit trails are immutable, archived with the batch record, and readable by reviewers in plain language.
verification_test: Change a recorded value -> audit shows who, when, old, new and reason; a failed login, a role change and a configuration change each appear in the system log; an archived batch restores with its complete audit trail.

clause: Q1d (spreadsheet formulas computing results or a calculated yield are dynamic content), Q3 (validated MPCR calculations), Q6 (electronic worksheets are controlled forms); binding basis 211.103, 211.188(b)(7), 211.68(b)
requirement: FDA gives spreadsheet formulas that compute results or a calculated yield as an example of dynamic record content (Q1d); workflow validation should show MPCR calculations are correct (Q3); electronic worksheets are forms to control (Q6). Binding: yields are determined at appropriate phases and, when an automated system under 211.68 computes them, one person independently verifies the result (211.103); the batch record states actual and percent-of-theoretical yield (211.188(b)(7)); computer input and output are checked for accuracy (211.68(b)).
system_implications: Yield and other GMP calculations run in validated, version-controlled eBMR logic, storing inputs, formula version and result; one person verifies each automated yield calculation as 211.103 requires; any external spreadsheet used for GMP calculations is a controlled template, retained natively with formulas intact as a dynamic record, not only as a printout.
verification_test: The yield step shows inputs, formula version, result and a verification signature; editing a formula outside change control is impossible; an attached spreadsheet is a controlled template version stored in native format.

requirement: For 211.68, 'computer or related systems' means more than software and servers: FDA includes attached devices, networks, cloud hosting, the people who operate the system and its documentation such as manuals and SOPs (drawing on an ANSI description of a system as people, machines and methods organized for set functions).
system_implications: Validation, access control, change control and backup scope for the eBMR cover the hosting/cloud and network layers, peripherals (balances, scanners, label printers, terminals), interfaces, user roles and training, and the SOPs/manuals. For SaaS or cloud hosting, assess the provider's controls over these layers and cover them contractually (design inference - Q1f names cloud infrastructure but does not detail supplier controls).
verification_test: The system inventory/validation plan lists hosting and cloud components, network, peripherals, interfaces, roles and SOPs, each with an owner and qualification evidence; a change to a hosting component is routed through change control.

requirement: When one system handles both CGMP and non-CGMP work, the firm should assess, and mitigate as appropriate, the chance that its non-CGMP features influence CGMP operations; the extent of validation should match the risk the automated system poses, and controls should address software, hardware, personnel and documentation.
system_implications: Documented impact assessment for non-GMP features (training or sandbox tenants, MBR simulation, planning/scheduling, analytics, ERP sync); their data segregated; they cannot write to GMP records, change GMP configuration or produce output that could be mistaken for GMP records (visible non-GMP marking).
verification_test: Attempt to write from the training/simulation area into a production batch record, or to reuse a real lot number there -> blocked; non-GMP outputs carry a non-GMP watermark; the impact assessment is in the validation package.

requirement: Manufacturers should set up and use a way of documenting which personnel are authorized on each CGMP computer system and with what privileges (e.g., a maintained list of authorized individuals), supporting the binding 211.68(b) duty that only authorized personnel make changes.
system_implications: The eBMR reports current and point-in-time users, roles, privileges and sites, with who granted or removed each privilege and when; access changes follow an approved request workflow; periodic access reviews record reviewer and outcome.
verification_test: Produce the access list as of a past date and reconcile it with access-request records; remove a leaver's access -> reflected in the list and the audit trail immediately.

clause: Inference from Q4 (technical restriction of settings changes; administrators independent of record content), Q12 (no change to required data without a record), Q1c; binding basis 11.10(e), 211.68(b)
requirement: The DI Q&A does not explicitly say who may switch audit trails off. It does recommend technically restricting who can change settings and reserving administrator rights over files and settings for people independent of record content (Q4), and it expects required data to be unchangeable without a record of the change (Q12); Part 11 requires secure, computer-generated audit trails of record creation, modification and deletion (11.10(e), binding). Together these mean audit trailing of GMP records should never be something that users responsible for record content can disable.
system_implications: GMP audit trail permanently on and not configurable per user, batch or step; any audit-scope setting changeable only by independent administrators through change control, with the change itself logged in a protected system log and flagged for QA review; no role that enters, verifies, reviews or releases GMP data holds that right.
verification_test: As a production or QA user, look for any function to disable or narrow audit trailing -> none exists; as administrator, change an audit-related setting -> requires a change-control reference and appears in the system log and the next periodic review.

requirement: Where the regulations fix no review frequency for a kind of data, derive the audit-trail review frequency from process knowledge and a risk assessment of data criticality, control mechanisms and product-quality impact, considering risks such as deletion, amendment or exclusion without authorization or detection; FDA's examples for risk-based review are logs of instrument status and communications, and alerts. The approach should meet CGMP and its reliability should be demonstrated.
system_implications: Capture and retain equipment/instrument interface logs (connection loss, message failures, retries), equipment status and alarm/alert records with the batch; a documented risk assessment sets their review frequency; events affecting a batch surface in that batch's review; the review-by-exception logic is validated and periodically challenged (e.g., comparing sampled full audit trails with the filtered view).
verification_test: Interrupt a balance or equipment interface during a step -> the event is recorded, linked to the batch and shown in review; the risk assessment defining frequency is on file; a periodic review record exists; a seeded unauthorized change is caught by the exception filter.

requirement: Copies of dynamic electronic records can count as true copies when held in the original format or in one that keeps content and meaning, as long as a suitable reader and copying equipment (software, hardware, media readers) stays readily available (211.180(d)); backups/archives are true copies with metadata kept for the whole retention period (Q1e).
system_implications: Archive plan covers the full retention period (at least one year after batch expiry under 211.180(a), longer if firm policy requires); keep a validated viewer or migrate to a format that preserves content, meaning, metadata and interactivity, verifying each migration; retiring a system requires a documented migration or read-only retention plan.
verification_test: Restore and interactively view the oldest retained batch (trends and audit trail included); a migration verification report shows record counts, checksums and sample comparisons.

clause: Q12 (data are a CGMP record when generated), Q10 (printouts as originals vs dynamic records), Q2 (same rules for paper and electronic); binding basis 211.180, 211.180(d), 211.188, 211.194
requirement: Data generated to meet a CGMP requirement are a CGMP record from the moment of generation (Q12). A printout or static record can be the original for devices such as balances and pH meters, and then it or a true copy must be kept (Q10, 211.180); dynamic electronic records cannot be replaced by printouts (Q10). Retention and review requirements do not differ between paper and electronic records (Q2).
system_implications: For each data type define the original: values keyed or captured in the eBMR are electronic originals and PDFs/prints are copies; device printouts that are originals are either retained and linked to the eBMR entry (reference number, reconciliation) or replaced by direct electronic capture; hybrid paper components get the same review and retention as the electronic record.
verification_test: The data-flow map for each MBR names the original record per data source; a weighing with a printed ticket shows the ticket linked and retained (or direct capture configured); a PDF export of the eBMR is marked as a copy.

clause: Q10 (second-person review of original lab records; microbiology plate-count example); binding basis 211.194(a)(8); for production steps 211.188(b)(11)
requirement: Original laboratory records, paper or electronic, must get second-person review so that all results and related information are properly reported (211.194(a)(8)); FDA's example is a contemporaneous written record of petri-dish colony counts that a second person then reviews.
system_implications: Manual readings entered in the eBMR (e.g., environmental monitoring plate counts, visual checks, manual gauge readings) are entered at the time of reading by the reader and verified by a different person; the record shows reader, verifier and both timestamps. For production steps the binding hook is 211.188(b)(11) (performer and checker identified).
verification_test: Enter a plate count -> second-person verification is required and the same user cannot verify their own entry; the record shows reader, verifier and timestamps.

clause: Q12 (no scrap-paper transcription), Q6 (controlled blank forms); binding basis 211.100(b), 211.160(a), 211.180(d), 211.186
requirement: Writing data on loose scraps that are thrown away once copied into the permanent record is not acceptable (Q12); blank forms that are used should be controlled and reconciled, with spoiled forms retained with justification (Q6).
system_implications: Provide a controlled contingency process for eBMR or network outages: pre-approved, uniquely numbered contingency forms issued under QU/document control; entries made on them at the time of performance; after recovery, the data are entered or attached as verified true copies, the paper originals retained, issued forms reconciled and the contingency period reviewed; no ad-hoc notes or personal devices.
verification_test: Simulate an outage: contingency forms are issued and logged; after recovery the batch shows the contingency period, linked scanned originals, reconciliation of issued forms and reviewer sign-off.

clause: Q12 (lab example: save each step or injection including aborted ones; aborted/incomplete injections audit-trailed, investigated, justified) - applied by analogy; binding basis 211.100(b), 211.188, 211.192
requirement: FDA expects processes designed so that required data cannot be changed without a record; in its chromatography example, data are written to durable media as each step or injection completes (incomplete or aborted ones included), and aborted or incomplete injections are captured in audit trails, investigated and justified.
system_implications: By analogy: aborted, cancelled or interrupted eBMR operations (abandoned weighings, cancelled label prints, aborted equipment cycles, restarted steps) are recorded with who, when and reason, remain visible in the batch record and need justification or investigation before step completion or release.
verification_test: Abort a weighing midway and restart -> both attempts recorded and the aborted one requires a reason; cancel a label print -> recorded and reconciled; the review view lists all aborted events.

clause: Q13 (applied by analogy to in-process testing); binding basis 211.160, 211.165, 211.188, 211.192, 211.194, 211.68(b)
requirement: Sampling or testing aimed at obtaining a particular result or overcoming an unacceptable one (so-called testing into compliance) conflicts with CGMP, and running actual samples in test, prep or equilibration runs to disguise it is violative. If an actual sample is used for system suitability, it should be a characterized secondary standard from a different batch, under written procedures. Every result, including plain mistakes and failing, suspect or passing values, has to stay in the retained CGMP records and be reviewed; invalidation needs an investigation with a documented, scientifically sound justification.
